title: AtomicProblem
description: A single, self-contained problem in a subdomain. Generated by the Atomic Problem Identification Pipeline. All string fields in English.

problem_id.description: Unique problem identifier. Format: <PREFIX>-<INDEX> where PREFIX is 5 uppercase characters derived from subdomain_label (E-02: simple labels → first 5 chars; compound labels → initials of content words, padded to 5). Collision suffix -A or -B appended when two subdomains share a prefix. INDEX is zero-padded to 4 digits, sequential per subdomain. Examples: ALGEB-0001, ALGDS-0042, NETZW-0007.

subdomain_id.description: Subdomain identifier from subdomains registry. Format: SD-NNN. Example: SD-001 for Algebra.

domain_id.description: Parent domain identifier. Format: D-NN. Example: D-01 for Mathematik.

parent_domain.description: Human-readable parent domain label in English. Example: Mathematics.

subdomain_label.description: Human-readable subdomain label in English. Example: Algebra.

title.description: Short, descriptive problem title in English. Must be self-contained and unambiguous. Max 80 characters.

problem_statement.description: Full, self-contained problem description in English. Must be solvable without external context unless requires_context is true. Should be precise enough that a correct answer exists or a clear evaluation rubric can be applied.

category.description: Thematic cluster within the subdomain. Normalized by 03_normalize (Title Case, English, soft normalization only — see E-04). Examples: Group Theory, Linear Algebra, Number Systems.

difficulty.description: Difficulty level relative to the subdomain. basic: introductory, testable at undergraduate entry level. intermediate: standard undergraduate. advanced: graduate or specialist. expert: research-adjacent or requires deep synthesis.

answer_type.description: Nature of the expected answer. factual: recall of a specific fact or definition. procedural: step-by-step application of a method. analytical: requires decomposition, proof, or derivation. evaluative: requires judgment, comparison, or trade-off assessment.

canonical_source.description: Authoritative reference for this problem. Should be a stable, widely recognised standard, textbook, or specification. Examples: ISO 80000-2, ICD-11, RFC 791, Knuth TAOCP Vol.1, DIN 8580.

verifiable.description: True if an automated checker could in principle validate the answer (e.g. the answer is a specific value, code output, or formal proof). False if evaluation requires human judgment.

hallucination_risk.description: Estimated risk that an LLM produces a plausible but incorrect answer. Derived from subdomain score: score >= 79 → low, score 55–78 → medium, score < 55 → high. Can be overridden by 04b_generation_review or 07_hallucination_scan.

requires_context.description: True if solving the problem requires a specific external document, dataset, case, or resource not embedded in problem_statement. False if the problem is fully self-contained.

tags.description: Free-form keywords for search and filtering. English only. Examples: ["complexity", "sorting", "worst-case"].

created_by.description: Pipeline run that produced this problem. Format: pipeline_vN/run_NNN. Example: pipeline_v1/run_001.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of problem creation (assigned in 08_finalization).

review_status.description: Current review state. All problems start as draft after 09_commit. Promotion to reviewed and approved is defined by the review workflow (see O-02 in engine.md).

$comment: Schema version 1.0.0. Decisions: E-02 (prefix schema), E-04 (category normalization), E-06 (hallucination_risk mapping). Open: O-02 (review workflow). See engine.md for full decision log.
